Intended for managed settings deployments that require sandboxing as a hard gate". That dropped half names the behaviour the key selects, and that behaviour is our permanent, non-configurable default. AGENTS.md warns about precisely this ("read the WHOLE line: several defects here hid in the second sentence").

(2) WRONG SUBSYSTEM for `enabled` (AGENTS.md trap 4, identically-purposed symbol in a sibling subsystem). Claude's `sandbox.enabled` is "Enable bash sandboxing (macOS, Linux, and WSL2)" — the Bash-tool sandbox. `SANDBOX_SETTING_KEYS` in sandbox-settings.ts governs a DIFFERENT subsystem: supervised-process isolation (ProcessSupervisor profiles none|read-only|workspace|networked|plugin-mcp|isolated-code). Our analogue of `sandbox.enabled` exists and is a live toggle: `macosSeatbeltBashSandboxEnabled` (packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:94, default false — the same default Claude documents), schema-declared (:182), validated (validators.ts:120/170/222), and read on BOTH backends via getMacosSeatbeltBashSandboxEnabled (storage.ts:1124) at claude-agent.ts:1319 and pi-agent.ts:3801. The finding looked in the wrong module.

(3) `failIfUnavailable` — ENFORCEMENT ONE LAYER UP. Its documented `true` behaviour (hard gate: refuse rather than run unsandboxed on missing dependencies or unsupported platform) is our unconditional default. There is no "warning + run unsandboxed" fallback anywhere: isolationUnavailable() throws from every backend and every unsupported case — isolation/linux.ts:33 (network launcher absent), :50 (filesystem launcher absent, and the comment states it is "Still REFUSED when no launcher exists"), and isolation.ts:244, :262, :341, :378, where :378 is the unsupported-platform default ("no process isolation backend exists for <platform>"). docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-26-sandbox-and-managed-policy.md:70-73 records the survey: "`process-isolation-unavailable` always throws, from seven sites ... no escape hatch". The key is absent because its only security-relevant value is permanently on; adding it could only WEAKEN the boundary.

(4) `credentials` — IMPLEMENTED, AND STRICTER THAN CLAUDE'S. Claude ships no built-in credential deny list (sandboxing.md:271, quoted verbatim in credential-deny-roots.ts:19-20). We ship an unremovable host-seeded floor: credentialDenyRoots() (session-tools-core/src/runtime/credential-deny-roots.ts:96, an evidence-cited list covering ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.netrc, ~/.docker, ~/.npmrc, ~/.kube, ~/.gnupg, keychains, browser cookie stores) composed inside the isolation funnel at isolation.ts:292-297 and :365 (`unconditionalDeniedReadRoots`), and passed as `credentialFloor` at bootstrap/managed-policy-resolution.ts:225. sandbox-settings.ts:806-812 records that the floor is deliberately RETAINED even when `filesystem.disabled` turns the layer off, because that key is user-scoped and would otherwise hand ~/.ssh, ~/.aws and the gateway token to every sandboxed command. sandbox-settings.ts:318-326 explicitly cites settings.md:200's `sandbox.credentials` tolerance row and applies it. So "does not exist" is wrong at the behaviour level; only the settings KEY is absent, by design, so no layer can drop an entry.

(5) `socatPath` — INAPPLICABLE, not missing. Socat is Claude's sandbox-proxy relay (sandboxing.md:60/:321, quoted at sandbox-settings.ts:849-850). We have no proxy: outbound network is one bit on every backend we ship, and NO_DOMAIN_FILTER (sandbox-settings.ts:869-872) carries the MEASUREMENT behind that — Seatbelt's compiler rejects every domain form including IP literals, unshare/firejail toggle the whole namespace, and the Windows profile has one network.enabled boolean. The per-domain proxy layer (R19) is deliberately parked. `socat` occurs in our source only in a shellguard test corpus and two docblocks. A path override for a binary we never spawn is not a gap.

(6) `autoAllowBashIfSandboxed` — DATED RECORDED DECISION with a reason, in the deviation register's source plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-deviation-unit-5.md:115, category `documented, not implemented`: "the documented default `true` is conditioned on `sandbox.enabled`, an opt-in Nessy has no analogue of: supervised-process isolation here is unconditional, so porting the default verbatim would auto-approve EVERY Bash command ... A settable-but-unread key would be the exact 'declared on one path, enforced on another' defect this series keeps finding, so no key was added". (Not in inert-worklist §3, which indexes inert identifiers rather than absent keys, but the same class: a decision with a written reason.)

Provenance note: this row is not an independent observation. It is verbatim docs/superpowers/specs/data/2026-07-31-doc-sweep-phase1.json:307-309 (duplicated at :3959-3961) — an unchallenged sweep row, which per AGENTS.md is the weakest evidence state.

HONEST RESIDUAL (the one part not refuted): `bwrapPath` alone is a genuine, small gap. The Linux backend resolves its launcher through applyFilesystemIsolation/applyNetworkIsolation and fails closed when none is found, so an administrator cannot point it at a bwrap outside PATH. That is a deployment-convenience gap on one platform, plus a separate diagnostics difference — Claude exits at STARTUP while we throw at SPAWN, and 2026-07-26-sandbox-and-managed-policy.md:76-79 already records "There is no startup capability probe". Neither supports the claim as filed, which asserts six absent keys as a missing capability.

Recorded at 2026-07-26-sandbox-and-managed-policy.md:70-73. Adding the key could only weaken the boundary. - `credentials` — IMPLEMENTED AND STRICTER. credentialDenyRoots() (session-tools-core/src/runtime/credential-deny-roots.ts:96) is seeded as an unremovable floor in the isolation funnel (isolation.ts:292-297, :365) and at managed-policy-resolution.ts:225, retained even under `filesystem.disabled` (sandbox-settings.ts:806-812). - `bwrapPath` — REAL BUT NARROW RESIDUAL. Linux resolves its launcher host-side and fails closed; an admin cannot override PATH detection.
